summary:
I'm Divyanshu, an applied AI engineer based in Exeter. I build software that helps people work through messy information and everyday tasks: finding an answer across documents, preparing a job application, or running a shop from a chat.

That takes different forms in my projects. DocChat brings PDFs, YouTube transcripts and web pages into one conversation, with citations and checks against the source material. JobFit connects job discovery, fit analysis and tailored application documents. SuperOps turns Telegram messages into inventory updates, bills and customer credit records for a kirana store. JARVIS brings voice, memory and permission-controlled tools to the Mac.

My foundation is three years of software engineering at Mphasis, working on banking and visa-processing systems, followed by an MSc in Statistical Data Science at Exeter. For my dissertation, I built EPC: a pipeline analysing 1.8 million housing energy records in South West England, combining policy analysis with predictive modelling. That mix of application development and statistical thinking shapes how I build AI today.

projects.name: JobFit
projects.summary: Job discovery, fit analysis and tailored application documents in one persistent workflow. Six specialist agents exchange validated outputs, stream progress and retry failed steps without starting over.

caseStudy.headline: From a job description to an application you can review.
caseStudy.problem: A job search means repeatedly comparing requirements, finding gaps and rewriting application materials. Keeping those steps connected matters as much as generating the text.
caseStudy.contribution: I built a two-phase workflow: parse the role, score the match and identify gaps, then generate resources, a cover letter and a tailored resume. Results persist in PostgreSQL and progress streams to the browser.
caseStudy.decision: Each agent returns a validated structure. Failed or missing steps can be retried under a database lock, so a failure in one stage does not require a complete rerun. Model tiers and per-call cost records make the cost of each stage inspectable.
caseStudy.outcome: The application supports saved analyses, document exports and resumable workflows. A cost report compares recorded model usage against an all-Sonnet baseline; savings depend on the workload.
caseStudy.limitation: The documented live evaluation has not yet been run. Deterministic fixtures check schemas and validators, not model quality. AWS deployment definitions remain in the repository, but that environment is shut down.
workflowDetails: Start with a candidate profile and a job description. The saved profile supplies the facts used to evaluate the role and draft application materials.
A job parser structures the role, a match scorer compares it with the profile, and a gap analyst identifies missing requirements. Each stage returns validated output.
Specialist agents produce resource recommendations, a cover letter and tailored resume content. Saved workflow state allows failed stages to be retried.
Review the analysis and application materials, then export documents. Progress streams to the browser and results remain available in saved analyses.

projects.name: DocChat
projects.summary: A source-grounded assistant for PDFs, YouTube transcripts and web pages. Retrieval experiments compare candidate approaches against the current default, with explicit quality gates before changing it.

caseStudy.headline: Answers you can trace back to your sources.
caseStudy.problem: A fluent answer is not enough when the relevant evidence is buried across documents and web pages. The system needs to retrieve the right passages and make the answer traceable.
caseStudy.contribution: I built a pipeline that plans the query, retrieves context, synthesizes an answer and checks it against the sources. I also built retrieval evaluation tooling to compare ranking strategies on the same questions.
caseStudy.decision: I tested hybrid BM25 + reciprocal rank fusion against the existing dense + overlap reranker. The more complex option performed worse on the larger evaluation, so I kept the existing default.
caseStudy.outcome: On 127 questions across 781 chunks from 14 sources, the production default achieved MRR 0.834 versus 0.761 for hybrid retrieval. The measured hybrid-minus-default difference was -0.073 (95% bootstrap CI: -0.114 to -0.035).
caseStudy.limitation: This measures retrieval ranking, not answer correctness. The additional 103 questions were LLM-generated and labels were not independently audited; these results do not establish performance on unseen customer documents.
workflowDetails: Bring PDFs, YouTube transcripts and web pages into a shared source collection. The question starts a pipeline that plans how to find supporting evidence.
Retrieve relevant source passages using dense search and overlap reranking. Evaluation compares alternatives before changing the default retrieval strategy.
Synthesize an answer from the retrieved context, then run a critic stage that checks the answer against that evidence before it surfaces.
Return an answer with citations so the reader can trace it back to the sources. Retrieval ranking and generated-answer correctness are evaluated separately.

projects.name: PromptOps
projects.summary: Prompt evaluation with experiment tracking, failure inspection and CI quality gates. In a local four-case support benchmark repeated three times per variant, explicit citation instructions improved citation compliance from 0/12 to 12/12 answers. This is a small development-set result, not a general accuracy claim.

projects.name: SuperOps
projects.summary: A Telegram assistant for a kirana store: stock, billing and customer credit. The model selects tools; deterministic code handles money, stock checks and transactional updates.

caseStudy.headline: Run shop operations from a conversation.
caseStudy.problem: Stock, bills and customer credit are connected operations. A conversational interface must preserve those relationships even when messages repeat or two actions compete for the same stock.
caseStudy.contribution: I built a Telegram workflow around scoped store tools, draft bills and PostgreSQL transactions. Prices and quantities come from tool results, while money is calculated in integer paise.
caseStudy.decision: The model can choose an operation, but it cannot bypass database checks. Finalizing a bill locks the relevant rows and updates stock and credit together. Tool-level idempotency protects against repeated calls.
caseStudy.outcome: The repository includes keyless replay checks and synthetic safety cases that invoke registered tools and assert database state. Access is invite-only, with each invite creating a separate store.
caseStudy.limitation: Synthetic replays test tool behavior, not live model quality. A live agent baseline has not been accepted. Diverging tool-call replays and several retail edge cases remain documented limitations.
workflowDetails: Send a stock, billing or credit request through Telegram. Store identity comes from the verified chat, so requests remain scoped to the correct shop.
The agent selects from store-specific tools. Prices, quantities and customer records come from tool results rather than model-generated values.
Code calculates money in integer paise and checks available stock. Finalizing a bill updates inventory and customer credit together in a database transaction.
Return the bill, stock update or credit result to the conversation. Repeated calls are protected by idempotency checks, with diverging replays documented as a limitation.
